criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
evidence: Purdue BuildingShapesZip4 feature FID 71 names Dick & Sandy Dauch Alumni Center at 403 W Wood Street.
Independent source-ring comparison found 109 unique GIS perimeter points and 109 shell XY positions; maximum nearest-point error is 0.00000146 m.
criteria.finding: Building identity and plan geometry are strongly and directly supported by the official Purdue GIS footprint.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
evidence: The independently calculated GIS polygon centroid is [241.198987, -618.185206] m; the asset placement origin differs by less than 1e-11 m.

The exported geometry remains in the expected local coordinate frame. The structural shell reproduces the source ring without rescaling; full asset bounds include a documented southward sign/landscape extension.
criteria.finding: Horizontal placement, orientation, and footprint scale are well supported. Decorative bounds extend beyond the GIS wall footprint as expected; height and exact architectural dimensions are separately uncertain.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: The saved Purdue GIS feature reports four levels and its level datum fields; Purdue’s historic building database describes the facility as three-story. Evidence explicitly preserves rather than guesses away this conflict.

The roof membrane is a separate 1,075-vertex surface with a 0.90 m crown above the structural cap. The roof profile/material now read as a subtle curved gray membrane in the R3 views, consistent with the cited exterior photo, but no measured section or roof schedule was found.
The 14.4 m shell top, 15.305 m roof crest, and overall height are estimates. The above-grade floor count remains provisional.
criteria.finding: R3 fixes the incorrect winding and flat striped roof presentation, but the roof curve and vertical dimensions are not measured, and the story-count conflict remains unresolved.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: The overview shows brick exterior, horizontal light courses, a projecting glazed entrance, approach flagpoles, and a readable freestanding identity sign; these features are supported by Purdue for Life and Home of Purdue building-specific photos.

The curved frontage and roof edge are present, but window subdivisions, facade bay rhythm, precise entry proportions, side elevations, and sign/landscape placement remain approximate. The interiors are schematic because the Archives floorplan was not retrieved.
criteria.finding: Recognizable brick-and-glass character and entrance/site identity are represented; facade details and interiors remain interpretive.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
evidence: Separate Blender 5.2.3 process reopened the requested exact SHA and found the expected Scene and scene-linked Asset_dauch_alumni_center collection, with 663 objects including 659 meshes.
The 29 used materials are node-based; no external image dependencies or zero-area mesh faces were found. The shell is closed and consistently wound with positive signed volume 25,313.66 m³.

Building evidence records source URLs, GIS feature ID, retrieval dates, coordinate method, changes, bounds, and unresolved limits. The absent archival floorplan and non-surveyed vertical dimensions remain documented.
criteria.finding: The library is portable and well documented. Master linkage and shared manifest refresh are outside this isolated asset grade; the bounds report is ready for coordinator integration.

findings: The 109 GIS footprint vertices align within 0.00000146 m and the asset origin matches the computed footprint centroid within 1e-11 m.
All 109 GIS shell side faces point outward; the closed shell has positive signed volume and correctly oriented top and bottom caps.
The roof is now modeled with an estimated curved crown and neutral-gray membrane. Its exact section, elevation, and upper facade levels lack measured documentation.

Purdue’s historic record says three-story while GIS reports four levels; this conflict remains explicitly unresolved. The rendered building remains recognizably brick-and-glass with a glazed entrance, flags, and sign, but facade rhythm and interior remain schematic.
